u0: Normal progress: no fall recovery is currently due, and no exit-without-box obligation is outstanding. The agent must still ensure that the box is held on the very next step after any fall, and that it is carrying the box when it reaches the exit. A fall starts an immediate recovery obligation; reaching the exit empty-handed starts a pending carrying obligation. With the box in hand at the exit and no recovery due, the stated conditions are satisfied.
u1: A box fall has just occurred, so the one-step recovery rule is active: the agent must be holding the box on the very next step. If it does, the obligation is cleared and normal progress resumes, including when it is at the exit with the box. If it is not holding the box on that required step, the fall was not answered in time and the task is irreversibly failed.
u2: An exit has been reached without the box while no fall was pending, so the requirement to be carrying the box at the exit remains outstanding. The obligation is cleared once the agent is holding the box; remaining empty-handed leaves it pending. If a fall occurs while the agent is empty-handed, the state becomes a combined exit-carrying and immediate-recovery obligation.
u3: A fall has just occurred while an exit-without-box obligation was already outstanding, and the agent is currently empty-handed. The next step must put the box back in hand; if it does, both the exit-carrying and fall-recovery obligations are cleared and normal progress resumes. If it remains empty-handed, the recovery is missed and the task is irreversibly failed.
u4: A mandatory recovery was missed: after the box fell, the agent was not holding it on the required next step. This permanently violates the fall-recovery requirement, so successful completion is no longer possible. The failure cannot be undone by later carrying the box or by reaching the exit.
